# Codecuri și motoare software concurente: lista completă a variantelor care se pot instala (domeniile G și H)

Data verificării: 07.10.2026.

**Ce am citit din repo.** Rapoartele existente (03-modele-voce-llm.md, 04-candidati-research.md, vision-robotics.md, CONTRACTE_V2.md) aproape că nu tratează codecurile. Despre motoarele 3D spun doar atât: nvblox când există GPU, RTAB-Map ca alternativă pe CPU, Hydra pentru graful scenei. CONTRACTE_V2 cere ca fiecare flux să-și declare codecul și precizia adâncimii. Mai cere ca o previzualizare comprimată să nu devină niciodată intrare metrică. Lista de mai jos completează rapoartele, nu le reia.

**Ce am verificat pe serverul 192.168.100.151** (doar citire):
- Procesorul are AVX2, AVX-VNNI, FMA și F16C. **Nu are AVX-512.**
- Nu are placă grafică integrată (lspci arată doar 2 plăci GA106 RTX 3060). Deci Intel QSV și VAAPI **nu se pot folosi**.
- Nu există pe server imagini Docker cu ffmpeg, Open3D sau OpenVINO. Toate trebuie construite.

**Cum se citesc etichetele:**
- **[V]** = verificat azi pe sursa primară din link.
- **[C]** = din cunoștințele mele, cu link oficial; trebuie reconfirmat la instalare, cu manifest și sha256.
- **„(estimare)”** = cifră nemăsurată pe acest CPU. Pentru benchmark rămâne not_run până o rulăm.
- **„Comercial”** se referă la drepturile de autor asupra codului. Patentele sunt notate separat.

---

## G. Codecuri

Calea implicită rămâne brută (raw). Codecurile sunt opțiuni. Cele cu pierderi sunt marcate **LOSSY**.

### Baza comună: FFmpeg
- **Licență:** LGPL-2.1+. Devine GPL dacă se construiește cu x264 sau x265. Nu există licență comercială „nici contra plată” [V] https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html
- **Versiuni disponibile pentru instalare în paralel** [V] https://ffmpeg.org/download.html:
  - 9.0.2 „Lei” (18.09.2026)
  - 8.1.3 (21.09.2026)
  - 8.0.3 (18.06.2026)
  - 7.1.5 (20.06.2026)
  - 6.1.6 (20.06.2026)
- **Propunere:** două imagini Docker.
  - **ffmpeg-lgpl**, pentru producție: libaom, SVT-AV1, dav1d, libvpx, libopus, libwebp, libjxl, FLAC/WavPack, libdav1d.
  - **ffmpeg-gpl**, pentru cercetare: adaugă x264 și x265.
  - Plus o versiune anterioară (7.1.5), pentru selectorul „Versiuni”.
- **Nu activa niciodată `--enable-nonfree`** (fdk-aac).

### Video, fără pierderi (verificare bit-exactă prin framemd5 în același format de pixeli; NV12 de la iPhone trebuie comparat tot ca NV12)

| Variantă | Licență | Comercial | CPU | Sursa |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw YUV/NV12 (implicit) | n/a | da | da | n/a |
| FFV1 (RFC 9043), nativ în FFmpeg | LGPL | da, fără patente | da; cu slices multithread, ~100+ fps la 1080p (estimare) | [V] ffmpeg legal |
| ffvhuff/HuffYUV, UtVideo (native în FFmpeg) | LGPL | da | da, foarte rapide | [C] https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-codecs.html |
| libaom AV1 `lossless=1` | BSD-2 + AOM Patent License 1.0 | da | lent | [C] https://aomedia.googlesource.com/aom |
| libvpx VP9 `-lossless 1` | BSD-3 | da | mediu | [C] https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx |
| x264 `-qp 0` / x265 `lossless=1` | GPL-2 | intern da; la redistribuire, GPL sau licență plătită | rapid | [V] https://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html; x265 [C] https://bitbucket.org/multicoreware/x265_git (pagina n-a răspuns, HTTP 429) |
| secvență de imagini PNG / JXL lossless | vezi secțiunea Imagini | da | da | n/a |

### Video, cu pierderi (LOSSY; pentru previzualizare, transport și arhivă secundară)

**AV1:**
- **SVT-AV1:** licență „Clear BSD” plus AOM Patent License 1.0, fără redevențe, reciprocă și cu terminare defensivă [V] https://gitlab.com/AOMediaCodec/SVT-AV1 și PATENTS.md.
- Pe CPU, cel mai bun raport viteză/calitate. Cu preset 8–10, 1080p, ~60–150 fps (estimare).

**AV1, alte implementări:**
- libaom (BSD-2 + AOM) [C].
- rav1e (BSD-2) [C] https://github.com/xiph/rav1e
- dav1d, doar decodor (BSD-2) [C] https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d

**VP9 și VP8:** libvpx, BSD-3, fără redevențe [C].

**H.264:**
- **x264:** GPL-2, cu licență comercială de la x264licensing@videolan.org [V].
- **OpenH264:** cod BSD-2 [V] https://github.com/cisco/openh264. Atenție: Cisco plătește redevențele MPEG LA numai pentru binarul descărcat de la Cisco la instalare. Dacă îl compilăm noi, plătim noi [V] https://www.openh264.org/faq.html. **Uz comercial: neclar din cauza patentelor.**

**HEVC/H.265:**
- **x265:** GPL-2 sau licență comercială MulticoreWare [C].
- **Kvazaar:** BSD-3, v2.3.2 (09.2025) [V] https://github.com/ultravideo/kvazaar
- Ambele rămân sub patentele HEVC (Access Advance/Via LA). **Neclar fără consultanță juridică.**

**VVC/H.266:**
- **VVenC:** BSD-3-Clause-Clear [V] https://github.com/fraunhoferhhi/vvenc. Integrarea în FFmpeg prin libvvenc și decodorul VVC nativ: [C].
- Patente VVC: neclar. Recomandat doar în setul de cercetare.

**MJPEG pentru previzualizare rapidă:** libjpeg-turbo (BSD-3/IJG/zlib) [C] https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo

**Encodere hardware:**
- **NVENC/NVDEC pe RTX 3060 (Ampere):** codează H.264 și HEVC; AV1 doar decodează [C]. Doar profil GPU: instalat, dar dezactivat cu motivul „driver NVIDIA neîncărcat”.
- **QSV/VAAPI:** nu se pot folosi (fără iGPU [V lspci]). Rămân pe dinafară.

**Pe iPhone (on-device):**
- VideoToolbox pentru H.264 și HEVC hardware. Patentele sunt acoperite de licența dispozitivului Apple [C].
- ProRes doar pe modelele Pro [C].
- AV1 doar la decodare, de la A17 Pro în sus [C].
- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/videotoolbox

### Imagini

| Variantă | Lossless | Licență | Sursa |
|---|---|---|---|
| PNG (libpng/zlib-ng; optimizare cu oxipng, MIT) | da | libpng/zlib | [C] http://www.libpng.org/pub/png/libpng.html |
| WebP lossless (libwebp) | da (și LOSSY) | BSD-3 | [C] https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libwebp |
| JPEG XL (libjxl, `distance 0` = lossless) | da | BSD-3 + acord suplimentar pe patente; minim v0.12 din motive de securitate | [V] https://github.com/libjxl/libjxl |
| AVIF lossless (libavif + aom/SVT) | da | BSD-2 | [C] https://github.com/AOMediaCodec/libavif |
| JPEG 2000 lossless (OpenJPEG) | da | BSD-2 | [C] https://github.com/uclouvain/openjpeg |
| QOI (foarte rapid) | da | MIT | [C] https://github.com/phoboslab/qoi |
| JPEG: libjpeg-turbo / mozjpeg / jpegli | LOSSY | BSD-3 (jpegli s-a mutat în google/jpegli [V]) | [V] libjxl README; [C] https://github.com/google/jpegli |
| HEIC (libheif; nativ pe iPhone) | LOSSY | LGPL-3 + patente HEVC | [C] https://github.com/strukturag/libheif |

### Audio

**Fără pierderi:**
- PCM float32/int16 (implicit).
- **FLAC:** libFLAC cu licență BSD-like; uneltele CLI sunt GPL [V] https://github.com/xiph/flac. Lucrează doar cu întregi, deci float32 nu este lossless fără conversie [C].
- **WavPack:** BSD-3, mod lossless și hibrid [V] https://github.com/dbry/WavPack. Lossless pe float32 [C], deci e potrivit pentru PCM f32.
- **ALAC:** Apache-2.0, nativ pe iOS [C] https://github.com/macosforge/alac
- **TTA:** decodor nativ în FFmpeg [C].
- Rămân pe dinafară: Monkey's Audio și OptimFROG (licențe restrictive sau proprietare).

**Cu pierderi (LOSSY):**
- **Opus (libopus):** BSD-3, fără redevențe; recomandarea pentru transport [C] https://opus-codec.org/license/
- **AAC, encoderul nativ FFmpeg:** LGPL; patentele AAC sunt neclare [C].
- **fdk-aac:** licență proprietară, incompatibilă cu GPL, fără licență de patente [V] https://github.com/mstorsjo/fdk-aac/blob/master/NOTICE. **Pe dinafară** (pentru FFmpeg e nonfree).
- **AAC Apple AudioToolbox** pe telefon [C].
- Vorbis (BSD) [C]. MP3 cu LAME (LGPL) [C]. Codec2 (LGPL-2.1, debit foarte mic) [C]. LC3 cu liblc3 (Apache-2.0) [C].

**Codecuri neurale (LOSSY, doar set de cercetare; nepotrivite pentru amprentele acustice ale echipamentelor):**
- **DAC (Descript):** MIT pentru cod și greutăți, 16/24/44,1 kHz, ~8 kbps [V] https://github.com/descriptinc/descript-audio-codec
- **EnCodec:** cod MIT [V] https://github.com/facebookresearch/encodec. Licența greutăților trebuie reconfirmată pe cardul HuggingFace.
- **Mimi (Kyutai):** greutăți CC-BY-4.0, cod MIT/Apache, 24 kHz, 1,1 kbps [V] https://github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi
- SNAC (MIT) [C]. Lyra v2 (Apache-2.0, TFLite, rulează pe CPU) [C].

### Adâncime

**Fără pierderi pe float32 brut:**
- raw f32 (implicit).
- **zstd:** dual BSD/GPLv2, alegem BSD; v1.5.7 [V] https://github.com/facebook/zstd
- **lz4:** BSD-2 pentru bibliotecă [C] https://github.com/lz4/lz4
- **Blosc2:** BSD; zstd/lz4/blosclz/zlib plus filtrele shuffle/bitshuffle/delta/bytedelta [V] https://github.com/Blosc/c-blosc2. Probabil cel mai bun pentru f32 (estimare).
- **fpzip:** BSD-3, lossless pe float [V] https://github.com/LLNL/fpzip
- **zfp, modul reversibil:** BSD-3, bit-exact, v1.0.1 [V] https://github.com/LLNL/zfp
- **OpenEXR** cu ZIP/PIZ/RLE pe float32: BSD-3 [V] https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr
- **TIFF** cu deflate și predictor float (libtiff) [C].
- **Pe iPhone:** framework-ul Apple Compression (LZFSE/LZ4/zlib/LZMA) [C] https://developer.apple.com/documentation/compression

**Cuantizate (lossless doar față de milimetrii uint16, nu față de f32; de etichetat clar):**
- **RVL:** suportat în ROS 2 compressed_depth_image_transport din v4.0.0 (13.04.2024) [V] https://index.ros.org/p/compressed_depth_image_transport și https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/p/compressed_depth_image_transport/__CHANGELOG.html. Plus implementarea din articolul Wilson 2017 (Microsoft) [C].
- **PNG pe 16 biți.**
- **zfp și SZ3 cu eroare limitată** (LOSSY) [C].

### Nor de puncte, mesh și splat

| Variantă | Lossless? | Licență | Sursa |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLY binar (implicit) | da | n/a | n/a |
| Draco v1.5.7 | quantization=0 păstrează valorile, dar **reordonează punctele**; altfel LOSSY (qp 11 recomandat) | Apache-2.0 | [V] https://github.com/google/draco |
| glTF/GLB + KHR_draco / EXT_meshopt_compression / KHR_mesh_quantization | depinde de cuantizare | specificații Khronos | [C] https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF |
| meshoptimizer v1.3 + gltfpack | codecul e lossless pe date deja cuantizate; simplificarea e LOSSY | MIT | [V] https://github.com/zeux/meshoptimizer |
| LAS/LAZ: LASzip | lossless față de întregii scalați din LAS | Apache-2.0 | [V] https://github.com/LASzip/LASzip |
| LAZ: laz-perf (și WASM) / COPC | idem | Apache-2.0 | [V] https://github.com/hobuinc/laz-perf |
| E57 (libE57Format) | da | BSL-1.0 | [C] https://github.com/asmaloney/libE57Format |
| USDZ / OpenUSD (exportul nativ RoomPlan) | da | Apache-2.0 modificat | [C] https://github.com/PixarAnimationStudios/OpenUSD |
| SPZ (Gaussian splats), v4 cu zstd, ~10x față de PLY | LOSSY | MIT | [V] https://github.com/nianticlabs/spz |
| Compresia octree din PCL | LOSSY | BSD-3 | [C] https://github.com/PointCloudLibrary/pcl |
| MPEG G-PCC (TMC13) / V-PCC | ambele moduri | licență ISO și patente: neclar, doar cercetare | [C] https://github.com/MPEGGroup/mpeg-pcc-tmc13 |
| OBJ | da (text) | n/a | n/a |

### Compresoare generale (pentru arhive și metadate)
- zstd, lz4, Blosc2 (vezi mai sus).
- brotli (MIT) [C].
- xz/LZMA (0BSD/domeniu public) [C].
- zlib-ng (zlib) [C].
- LZFSE (BSD-3) [C].

## H. Motoare software

### H1. Reconstrucție 3D și fuziune volumetrică

**Rulează pe CPU, licență permisivă (pentru producție):**
- **Open3D (MIT).** Variante selectabile:
  - ScalableTSDFVolume (legacy, CPU)
  - UniformTSDFVolume
  - VoxelBlockGrid (tensor; CPU, CUDA sau SYCL)
  - pipeline-ul offline RGB-D cu ColoredICP
  - meshing: Poisson / Ball pivoting / marching cubes
  - Versiuni în paralel: **0.19.0 și 0.20.0 (16.09.2026)**. Versiunea 0.20 aduce randare de Gaussian splats (PLY/SPLAT/SPZ), TSDF pe SYCL Intel (irelevant aici), Python 3.10–3.14 și un wheel mai mic cu ~335 MB [V] https://github.com/isl-org/Open3D/releases
- **VDBFusion:** MIT, se instalează cu `pip install vdbfusion`, bazat pe OpenVDB [V] https://github.com/PRBonn/vdbfusion
- **supereight2:** BSD-3, CPU (TBB opțional); TSDF, MultiresTSDF, MultiresOccupancy [V] https://github.com/smartroboticslab/supereight2
- **wavemap:** BSD-3; testat pe CPU Intel/AMD/ARM sub Ubuntu 20.04/22.04/24.04; interfață ROS1, API Python, Docker [V] https://github.com/ethz-asl/wavemap
- **RTAB-Map:** licență BSD; Docker `introlab3it/rtabmap` [V] https://github.com/introlab/rtabmap. Construcția trebuie făcută **fără module nonfree**: SURF e nonfree; patentul SIFT a expirat și SIFT e în OpenCV ≥4.4 [C]. Pe CPU face odometrie RGB-D, loop closure și export de nori și mesh. Este candidatul CPU cel mai complet.
- **Voxblox:** BSD-3, ROS1 [V] https://github.com/ethz-asl/voxblox. Fezabil doar într-un container ROS Noetic (EOL 05.2025) [C], deci variantă moștenită.
- **Kimera-Semantics:** BSD-2, construit peste Voxblox, ROS1; ultima revizie majoră în 2019 [V] https://github.com/MIT-SPARK/Kimera-Semantics. Variantă moștenită, pentru cercetare.
- **Hărți de ocupare pentru navigație:** OctoMap (BSD-3), UFOMap (BSD-3), Bonxai (MPL-2.0) [C].

**Cercetare sau licență restrictivă (pot rula pe CPU, dar NU în setul de producție):**
- **OpenCV KinFu / ColoredKinFu / LargeKinfu / DynaFu (opencv_contrib rgbd):** cer **OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE** din cauza patentelor KinectFusion; README-ul recomandă consultanță juridică [V] https://github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib/tree/4.x/modules/rgbd. **Comercial: NU fără clarificare juridică.**
- **InfiniTAM v3:** Oxford University Innovation Academic License, necomercial. Partea CPU se poate compila fără CUDA. Ultima versiune majoră: 2017 [V] https://github.com/victorprad/InfiniTAM (licența prin căutare web: https://toscode.gitee.com/jiajiewu/InfiniTAM).

**Doar profil GPU (instalate, dar oprite cu motivul „driver NVIDIA neîncărcat”):**
- **nvblox:** Apache-2.0, plus BSD-3 pentru fișierele preluate din Voxblox; necesită CUDA, fără variantă CPU [V] https://github.com/nvidia-isaac/nvblox și LICENSE.md.
- **ElasticFusion:** necomercial, CUDA (GPU de 3,5+ TFLOPS), neîntreținut [V] https://github.com/mp3guy/ElasticFusion. Cercetare și GPU.
- **Kintinuous** (necomercial), **BundleFusion** (CUDA), **PCL KinFu/KinFu-LS** (BSD, dar modulul CUDA e vechi și are aceleași patente KinectFusion): toate [C], cercetare și GPU.

## Recomandare pentru matricea de licențe

**Set implicit pentru producție (100% permisiv, fără patente cunoscute):**
- **Video:** raw, FFV1, UtVideo/ffvhuff, AV1 (SVT-AV1, libaom, rav1e, dav1d), VP9 (libvpx).
- **Imagini:** PNG, WebP-L, JXL, AVIF-L, QOI, J2K-L.
- **Audio:** PCM, FLAC, WavPack, ALAC, Opus.

Official-source rule vs. planned runtimes: faster-whisper (CTranslate2), whisper.cpp GGML, Parakeet/wespeaker/3D-Speaker 'via sherpa-onnx' normally pull third-party conversions (Systran/*, ggerganov/*, csukuangfj/*), which rule 6 forbids. Either require our own conversion from openai/whisper and nvidia/* checkpoints with a parity test, or list the backend-author conversions as an explicit, documented exception with sha256.

On-device and app distribution is outside the matrix. GET /api/app/settings selects transport/local-recording codecs and ondevice.* engines (D18), but S4 accepts license as optional, ondevice engines are not subject to the production/research gate, and there is no 'distributed in iOS app' column. App Store distribution makes LGPL/GPL (FFmpeg, LASzip, x264) and CC-BY/Apache NOTICE obligations apply. Make license mandatory for ondevice engines, apply D10 to them, and add a phone-side codec/library licensing row set (VideoToolbox H.264/HEVC covered by Apple, libopus, libjxl, Draco, zstd, etc.).

Audio benchmarking relies on ESC-50 (CC-BY-NC-3.0), and the result drives production decisions (ensemble activation, best-per-class). Using it to choose models for a commercial product is arguably not non-commercial use. Add a permissive audio eval set, e.g. an FSD50K subset filtered to CC0/CC-BY clips (with attribution), so the production gate does not depend on an NC dataset. The spec also asks for ODinW, which is missing from §5; its sub-datasets have mixed licenses and must be listed individually.

Face re-ID rows: reid_face.sface (OpenCV Zoo) is marked commercial=yes, but its training-data lineage (MS-Celeb-1M/CASIA-derived face sets were withdrawn or are research-only) is not checked. It should be E/unclear. Biometric processing is also GDPR Art. 9, so the matrix should require an explicit DPIA/owner gate, not just 'oprit implicit'.

sha256 pinning is trust-on-first-use. Where the publisher provides hashes (HF LFS oid sha256, GitHub release asset digests, Zenodo md5/checksum), cross-check them on --pin and record publisher_hash in the manifest. For Google Drive sources (RT-DETRv4, DEIM), also record the README commit that links the file.

Smaller lineage points to verify at pin: torchvision weights (the docs disclaim dataset-derived permission), Florence-2 FLD-5B (built from specialist-model pseudo-labels, so check the O365 lineage), EfficientAT (distilled from PaSST, which is fine but should be noted), and OpenCLIP/CLAP 'unclear' needs a concrete decision criterion. Also say where end-user-facing attribution for CC-BY-4.0 weights (Parakeet, Canary, PANNs) is shown (site/app About), not only in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

[Izolare/evaluator, BLOCANT] §9.1 spune ca evaluatorul trimite cererile PRIN model-server si ca la rulare sunt incarcate doar motorul masurat si membrii ansamblului. §1.2 spune ca eval ruleaza doar cu model-server oprit. Cele doua se contrazic. In plus, descarcarea motoarelor de productie pentru masurare ar opri scene-recon/scene-audio, iar motoarele dezactivate (load_policy=manual) ar trebui incarcate fara a atinge starea dorita sau auditul. Solutie: o instanta separata `model-server-eval` (aceeasi imagine, proiect/retea proprie, buget propriu, configuratie de evaluare care nu vine din model_engine_desired). Asta trebuie scris explicit si legat de T8.

[CPU hibrid, BLOCANT pentru masuratori] i9-12900KF are 8 P-core (CPU 0-15, 5.1-5.2 GHz) si 8 E-core (CPU 16-23, 3.9 GHz), verificat cu lscpu. `cpus: 8` este doar cota CFS, fara pinning. Firele intra-op ORT (8 pe motor, impartire statica) ajung amestecate pe P si E, iar firele de pe E-core intarzie toata inferenta. p50/p95 devin nereproductibile, iar toleranta de ±20% va fi depasita frecvent. Trebuie: `cpuset` declarat pentru model-server si eval (ex. P-core 8-15, dupa ce verificati ce folosesc containerele live), threads ≤ numarul de nuclee din cpuset, cpuset inregistrat in host{} din benchmark, plus o regula ca latenta se masoara numai cu cpuset fix.

[Fire ascunse] Doc-ul fixeaza doar intra_op_num_threads / INFERENCE_NUM_THREADS / cpu_threads. In cgroup, os.cpu_count() intoarce tot 24, deci OpenVINO (streams/affinity), inter_op ORT, numpy/OpenBLAS/MKL/OMP, torch.set_num_threads si CT2 inter_threads/num_workers isi aleg singure 24 de fire per proces. Cu N procese de motor, suprasubscrierea reala este mult peste plafonul de 1.5x din §5.4. Trebuie impus in fiecare proces de motor: OMP_NUM_THREADS / OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS / MKL_NUM_THREADS = threads, inter_op=1, OpenVINO NUM_STREAMS=1 + ENABLE_CPU_PINNING conform cpuset, apoi verificat intr-un test (numarul de fire din /proc/<pid>/status ≤ threads + o marja mica).

[Memorie/OOM] (a) Admiterea nu acopera varful din timpul load/optimizarii de graf (ORT/OpenVINO pot ajunge la 2-3x RSS-ul final), deci T4 poate esua tocmai la incarcare. Trebuie un factor de varf in manifest (ram_mb_peak_load) sau masurat. (b) Nu exista mecanism care sa garanteze ca, la OOM in cgroup, kernelul omoara procesul motorului si nu gateway-ul. Setati oom_score_adj=1000 pe procesele copil (permis fara privilegii); T4 sa verifice ca gateway-ul supravietuieste. (c) tmpfs /tmp 512m se contorizeaza in memoria cgroup-ului si trebuie scazut din buget. (d) Pe host swap-ul e plin (7/7 GB) si sunt ~57 GB disponibili. Setati memswap_limit = mem_limit pe toate serviciile, altfel containerele pot impinge productia in swap. (e) Toate profilele pornite simultan inseamna 24+16+8+4+16 = 68 GB, peste ce e disponibil. Trebuie un garant global intre containere (sau o regula exclusiva de profil), nu doar bugetul per container.

[Preprocesare in gateway] Gateway-ul este un singur proces async (GIL) care face micro-batching. Nu e specificat unde ruleaza conversia YUV→RGB 1920x1440, letterbox-ul, resample_poly si encodarea RLE. Daca ruleaza in gateway, serializeaza toate motoarele si strica latenta; in plus, transferul de cadre de 4 MB prin Pipe/pickle costa. Precizati ca pre- si post-procesarea ruleaza in procesul motorului si ca transferul se face prin shared_memory.

[Fuziune: supra-ajustare] val-A are 250 de imagini COCO si pe el se invata ponderi WBF si calibrare Platt/temperatura PER (model, clasa) pentru 80 de clase, plus best_per_class pe AP-ul per clasa. Multe clase au < 5 instante in 250 de imagini, deci ponderile si alegerea per clasa sunt zgomot (winner's curse). Trebuie: suport minim per clasa (ex. ≥ 20 GT) cu revenire la ponderi globale, regularizare/shrinkage spre ponderea globala, si un subset de validare mai mare pentru invatare (ex. 2000 de imagini val2017, cu testul disjunct).

[Fuziune: testare repetata] Poarta D12 se aplica pe acelasi val-B pentru fiecare combinatie incercata (moduri × submultimi de membri × ponderi), iar §6.4 re-testeaza la fiecare benchmark nou. Asta duce la forking paths si la supra-ajustare pe val-B in timp. Trebuie: bootstrap explicit PERECHE (aceleasi imagini reesantionate pentru ansamblu si individual), alegerea celui mai bun individual pe val-A (nu max pe val-B), corectie pentru comparatii multiple (Holm/Bonferroni pe numarul de configuratii testate) sau un test final tinut deoparte si folosit o singura data, plus numarul de configuratii incercate notat in evidence.

[Fuziune audio] ESC-50 are 5 folduri oficiale, dar doc-ul invata T_m/w_m pe un 'val-A' nedefinit. Trebuie validare incrucisata pe folduri (invatare pe 4, test pe 1), cu raportare medie ± abatere. Excludeti checkpoint-urile fine-tunate pe ESC-50 (AST/BEATs/PaSST au variante ESC), altfel apare scurgere. Precizati top-1 ca argmax restrans la clasele mapate. Fuziunea pe grila de 0.48 s amesteca scoruri la nivel de clip (AST 10 s, repetat pe 20 de cadre) cu scoruri la nivel de cadru; pentru benchmark-ul ESC-50 fuziunea trebuie definita la nivel de clip (5 s) si declarata.

[Fuziune: scoruri fara semantica] Florence-2, Qwen3-VL, Kosmos-2 si moondream nu produc scoruri de incredere per caseta. Pentru ei AP si calibrarea Platt sunt nedefinite, iar WBF nu poate pondera. Interfata trebuie sa declare `score_semantics: probability|logit|none` in manifest si in result, sa specifice ce scor primesc acesti membri (excludere din AP / AP la un singur prag / doar Acc@0.5 pe RefCOCO) si sa interzica intrarea lor in WBF fara calibrare.

[Interfata: mapare multi-la-unu] label_space=coco80 pentru modelele O365/LVIS mapeaza mai multe clase native pe o singura clasa COCO (ex. mai multe tipuri de cana/pahar). Nu e definita agregarea scorurilor si caseta la coliziune (max? NMS intra-model dupa mapare?). Asta afecteaza atat AP-ul masurat, cat si fuziunea. Regula trebuie fixata in contract si versionata impreuna cu labelmap_sha256.

[Provenienta] (a) labelmap_sha256 apare doar in result la detect/classify_audio. Trebuie si in provenance, inclusiv la membrii ansamblului. (b) Pentru ansamblu, model_id = 'ensemble:<task>@<versiune ponderi>' nu identifica membrii. Ce persista consumatorii (scene_observations.model_id) trebuie sa includa un ensemble_id = hash(metoda + parametri + engine_id@version + manifest_sha256 ai membrilor). (c) Lipsesc din provenance parametrii efectivi aplicati (score_threshold, mode, language, beam) si sha256 al intrarii (optional), fara de care o observatie nu poate fi reprodusa. (d) Parametrul `version` explicit dintr-o cerere poate declansa un load la cerere de catre orice consumator, ocolind starea dorita a adminului. Trebuie interzis (sau permis doar pentru caller=evaluator) si auditat.

[Reproductibilitate evaluator] (a) Masurarea acuratetei cu ORT_DISABLE_ALL, dar a latentei/productiei cu optimizari, inseamna ca cifrele afisate in UI nu descriu configuratia care ruleaza. Masurati acuratetea si latenta in configuratia de productie si verificati determinismul acolo (ORT CPU cu fire fixe este de regula determinist). (b) 'pycocotools / faster-coco-eval' trebuie fixat pe o singura implementare si versiune (pot diferi la a treia zecimala). (c) Unitatile AP sunt amestecate: pragurile '+0.5 AP' si toleranta '0.1 AP' presupun scara 0-100, iar pycocotools intoarce 0-1. Declarati scara in schema eva.benchmark/1. (d) Common Voice ro este distribuit acum cu acces gated (cont + acceptarea termenilor); se aplica regula de acceptare de catre proprietar, ca la seturile gated. (e) Pentru latenta: inregistrati in host{} cpuset-ul, guvernorul de frecventa si temperatura daca e disponibila, si separati overhead-ul HTTP/base64 de infer_ms in raport.

[Fezabilitate CPU in bugetul de 20 GB] Mai multe motoare marcate 'cpu-lent' nu incap fp32 in bugetul model-server alaturi de altele, de exemplu Qwen3-VL-4B fp32 la circa 16 GB si Canary-1B sau Whisper large-v3 la cativa GB. Matricea trebuie sa noteze, per motor, varianta de precizie fezabila (int8/fp16 OpenVINO, CT2 int8). Un motor cu ram_mb_est > buget trebuie sa apara canEnable=false cu motivul memory_budget_exceeded inca de la listare, nu abia la incercarea de pornire.

[Minor/auth] isEnginesAdmin: 'daca user.role exista' -> rol, altfel email. Daca dupa merge-ul 012 authStore.userForToken nu populeaza `role` pe obiectul user (/api/auth/me intoarce doar {id,email} in ADMIN_ARHITECTURA), verificarea cade silentios pe lista ENGINES_ADMIN_EMAILS. Trebuie un mod explicit (env ENGINES_AUTH_MODE=role|emails) si un test pentru fiecare mod, ca sa nu existe o cadere tacita.

Revizia r1 a arhitectului este comisă și urcată ca d6bbeca pe feat/models (clona ~/work/3dscan-models; pull --rebase fără conflicte, fără force). Au fost editate 3 fișiere: Site/docs/MODELE_ARHITECTURA.md, Site/docs/MODELE_INTERFATA.md și Site/docs/MODELE_LICENTE.md (+466/-141 linii). Am tratat toate cele 18 puncte vizibile din audit; tabelul cu rezolvări este în §19.1 din MODELE_ARHITECTURA.md. Lista primită era trunchiată în mijlocul punctului 18 ('Preprocesare in gateway ... in plus'), deci eventualele puncte de după nu au putut fi tratate. Asta e notat explicit în document.

Licențe. Regula este acum unică (MODELE_LICENTE §0.1). Steagurile de lineaj sunt: o365_direct, o365_pseudo (tratat la fel ca o365_direct, cu motivul scris), teacher_custom_license, gated_terms, custom_license, nc_data_source și face_data_withdrawn. Ce s-a mutat în research/unclear: OWL-ViT v1, OWLv2 (care era implicitul OV de producție), Kosmos-2, Florence-2 (până la verificarea adnotatorilor FLD-5B), RT-DETRv4 (scos și din on_demand), pyannote (segmentation-3.0, 3.1, community-1), SFace și AuraFace. Licența DINOv3 am citit-o pe sursă: permite uz comercial, cu interdicții de uz, Trade Controls și obligația de a transmite acordul la redistribuire. Nu e clar dacă un student distilat (RT-DETRv4) e 'derivat', de aceea rămâne unclear.

Au fost definite mai multe mecanisme noi:
- **Tranziția unclear→production (§0.2):** notă de aprobare în repo, plus legal_review approved cu by/at/ref/covers în același commit. Validatorul respinge orice altă combinație.
- **Acceptarea riscului rezidual (§0.3):** clase R-IMAGENET, R-AUDIOSET, R-UNDISCLOSED, R-WEB-CRAWL, R-SA1B și R-PATENT, acceptate o singură dată și auditat (E12, tabelul model_license_acceptance, funcția isLicenseApprover). Setul nu se mai numește '100% permisiv'.
- **Politica research (§0.4):** motoarele research rulează doar pe eval/replay (X-Eva-Purpose plus lista MODELS_RESEARCH_CALLERS). Rezultatele sunt în carantină (fără sincronizare în inventar/worldmodel/exporturi) și se pot purja după license_set. Implicitul unei sarcini și membrii unui ansamblu live sunt doar production.
- **Conversii (§0.5):** conversie proprie din checkpoint-urile openai/nvidia, cu paritate. Conversiile Systran, ggerganov sau csukuangfj sunt permise doar ca excepții documentate în §9.
- **Biometrie (§0.6):** sarcina nouă reid_face și poarta DPIA (GDPR art. 9).
- **G-iOS:** rândurile pentru bibliotecile distribuite prin App Store. LASzip, FFmpeg și x264 sunt excluse din aplicație. Licența devine obligatorie în S4.
- **Seturi de poartă cu licență comercială:** FSD50K eval filtrat CC0/CC-BY pentru audio, COCO/LVIS filtrate pe licența per imagine (4-8), ODinW-13 per sub-set. ESC-50 și RefCOCO rămân doar informative.
- **publisher_hash la --pin:** din HF lfs.sha256, digest-ul asset-ului GitHub și checksum-ul Zenodo. Pentru Google Drive: tofu plus commit-ul README și ID-ul fișierului.
- **Atribuirea vizibilă:** pagina /licente/ pe site și ecranul iOS 'Setări → Despre → Licențe terțe'.

Blocantul B-LIC-1. Workerul live rulează dfine_m_obj365, deci producția e neconformă din perspectiva licenței chiar azi. Recomandarea: trecerea pe detect.dfine.m-coco plus Detic (LVIS) pentru clasele din afara COCO, sau o acceptare scrisă a riscului de către proprietar. Termen: 2026-10-14 sau înaintea oricărui deploy, oricare vine primul. Auditul 10/10 nu se închide până la decizie.

Infrastructură:
- **Evaluator:** instanță separată model-server-eval, în proiectul 3dscan-models-eval, cu rețea, buget și cpuset proprii. Configurația vine dintr-un plan de evaluare, nu din model_engine_desired, iar instanța nu atinge starea dorită sau auditul. E legată de T8. model-server-ul care deservește consumatorii nu își mai descarcă motoarele pentru evaluare.
- **CPU hibrid:** topologia e verificată cu lscpu (P-core CPU 0-15, E-core CPU 16-23). Niciunul din cele 134 de containere nu are cpuset, iar loadavg era ~19,6. Am fixat cpuset per serviciu: model-server 8-15, eval 0-7, codec și tools 16-23. threads ≤ numărul de CPU din cpuset. Latența publicată sau folosită în porți e doar cea măsurată pinned.
- **Fire:** în fiecare proces de motor sunt fixate OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL, ORT inter_op=1 fără spinning, OpenVINO NUM_STREAMS=1 cu pinning condiționat, torch și CT2. Verificarea e în T19.
- **Memorie:** admitere pe ram_mb_peak_load (implicit 2,5×), oom_score_adj=1000 pe procesele motoarelor, tmpfs scăzut din buget (budget 14336 MB pentru mem_limit 16g), memswap_limit = mem_limit și un garant global de 40 GB (up.sh + stack_guard.sh, cu excluderi între profile; T4 și T22).
- **Gateway:** nu mai face calcul pe date (D20). Decodarea, YUV→RGB, letterbox, resample, batching-ul și RLE se fac în procesul motorului, fuziunea în procesul fusion. JSON e limitat la 4 MB, forma binară la 64 MB (T24).

Teste noi: T19-T24. Nimic nu a fost rulat: e doar documentație, iar toate cifrele de latență și acuratețe rămân not_run. N-am atins nimic din live (checkout, containere, DB) și nu am făcut prune.

[Memory accounting, ARH 5.4/D21] Admission and the post-warm-up check use per-process RSS from psutil, but the real limit is the cgroup (mem_limit 16g). RSS counts shared pages (libonnxruntime, libopenvino, numpy, read-only weights) once in every spawned engine process, so the sum overestimates. The cgroup, meanwhile, also counts page cache from reading model_store and the tmpfs, so the two never match. Fix: base the budget on cgroup memory.current/memory.stat (anon + shmem) for the container and on PSS/USS per process for attribution. Also count a fixed baseline per spawned process (Python + ORT/OV import, roughly 150-300 MB), which ram_mb_est does not cover.

[Memory, ARH 5.4/5.5] Warm-up uses 'inputs: 3' at an unspecified batch size. ORT's CPU arena (enable_cpu_mem_arena) and OpenVINO grow with batch and input size, so a later batch at max_batch=4, or a 1920x1440 frame, pushes RSS above the value measured after warm-up. The admission check then passes on a false number. Fix: warm-up must run at max_batch with the largest declared input. Alternatively set enable_cpu_mem_arena=false or arena_extend_strategy=kSameAsRequested and declare which.

[Production isolation, ARH 1.2] The global guard caps only memory (40 GB). There is no CPU cap for the whole models stack: the cpus quotas allowed together reach model-server 8 + ort-next 4 + torch 6 + codec 4 + eval 8+2 + fetch/export 4, well over 24 threads on a host with loadavg 10-19 and 129 running containers. There is also no cpu_shares/cpu weight lower than production and no pids_limit (each engine is a spawned process with thread pools). Fix: add MODELS_STACK_CPU_CAP (for example 12 cpus total) to stack_guard.sh, cpu_shares around 256 on every models* service so production wins under contention, and pids_limit per service. Optionally add blkio/device_write_bps for models-fetch during install_all (80-120 GB of downloads).

[Production isolation, ARH 9.1/15] eval_net is said to reach only the TEST DB. For production use (E7 queues jobs from the UI, and model_benchmarks rows feed the UI) the doc does not say how models-eval reaches the LIVE DB without attaching the live db container to eval_net, which would mean modifying a live container. Specify the production path. For example, the harness writes JSON to a volume and a one-shot models-provision in the main project imports it, or a dedicated, explicitly documented network.

[Provenance, INTERFATA 2.2] Provenance has no code version for the adapter, preprocessing or postprocessing (git commit of model-server plus image digest, and adapter version). manifest_sha256 only fixes the weights and export options, so a change in letterbox, NMS or postprocess changes outputs while provenance stays identical. Add provenance.server_build {git_sha, image_digest} and adapter_version, and add them to the eva.benchmark/1 JSON.

[Provenance, ensemble] For an ensemble, engine_id='ensemble:<task>' and version='version of the weights file'. manifest_sha256 is not defined for this case, yet consumers (10.1/10.2) persist only engine_id@version + manifest_sha256 + license_set. Persisted observations therefore cannot identify the member combination and member versions. Define a deterministic composite_sha256 = H(canonical-json of {fusion.method, params, weights_file_sha256, members[].manifest_sha256, server_build}), require it in provenance, and make consumers persist it (or members[]).

[Score semantics, INTERFATA 3.2/4.2] An ensemble returns calibrated scores (temperature/Platt), while a single engine returns raw scores. Consumer thresholds (score_threshold 0.25/0.3 in scene-recon) silently change meaning when the admin switches the default or turns an ensemble on or off from Settings. Add result.score_semantics: 'raw|calibrated@<file_sha>', and preferably apply the val-A calibration to the single default engine as well, so a switch from the selector does not change the threshold semantics.

[Fusion statistics, ARH 6.1] Per-(model, class) WBF weights learned by coordinate ascent on AP, per-class Platt calibration and per-class best_per_class selection all run on val-A = 250 COCO images. Many of the 80 classes have 0-5 instances in 250 images: per-class AP is undefined (pycocotools gives -1 and drops the class) or pure noise, so the per-class choice is overfitting. Fix: (a) stratify the val-A/val-B split so every class has at least N instances, or increase the subset (all COCO val2017 images with licenses 4-8, roughly 2k, are cheap on CPU); (b) shrinkage: global weights, with per-class weights or choices only for classes with at least N_min instances, otherwise fall back to global; (c) report how many classes were excluded.

[Fusion statistics, ARH 6.4] The ensemble gate does not specify that the bootstrap is PAIRED (the same resampled images for the ensemble and for the best individual, inside each resample), nor whether max_m metric(m) is recomputed in each resample or fixed on val-A. It also ignores multiple comparisons: several modes (wbf, best_per_class, wbf_best_per_class) times member subsets are tried against the same val-B, and choosing the winner on val-B creates a winner's curse. Fix: choose the configuration only on val-A, test exactly one candidate per task on val-B (or apply a Holm/Bonferroni correction), use a paired bootstrap with at least 2000 resamples (or BCa) and a fixed seed, and fix the best individual on val-A.

[Fusion statistics, ARH 6.4] The automatic switch to best_single when 'a new benchmark contradicts' an active ensemble has no hysteresis. With 250 images and a ±0.1 AP re-run tolerance, the ensemble can flip back and forth from noise. Define the disable rule as, for example, a CI95 upper bound below 0 on a new, full run, not just Δ < min_gain.

[Audio fusion, ARH 6.3] (a) CLAP zero-shot produces cosine similarities, softmax-normalized over the prompts, not independent sigmoid logits, so σ(T·logit) is ill-defined for it. Specify an affine calibration on the similarity (a·s+b, global or per class with shrinkage). (b) The audio gate measures at clip level on FSD50K, while live serving fuses on a 0.48 s grid by max-pooling AST's 10 s window, which smears it in time. The gate does not validate the frame-level fusion actually served. Either declare the fusion clip-level only, or add a frame-level evaluation (for example strong labels from AudioSet-strong, informative only). (c) FSD50K has 200 classes, so the gate must state that it evaluates only the intersection with the 527 (or 521 for YAMNet) and how hierarchical propagation of parent labels is handled. (d) MS-CLAP declares FSD50K among its training data (MODELE_LICENTE l.248), so it is contaminated on the gate set. Add a mandatory per-model overlap check between training and evaluation sets (Freesound IDs for FSD50K; COCO val2017 image IDs present in the training of LVIS/O365-based models).

[Reproducible evaluation, ARH 9.5] 'ORT_DISABLE_ALL for nondeterministic optimizations' contradicts 'the same code path as production' (9.1). Accuracy measured without graph optimizations is not the accuracy of the production session, and if the same setting is used for latency, the published latency is not production latency either. ORT CPU with fixed threads and ORT_SEQUENTIAL is already deterministic run to run. Fix: evaluate with exactly the production SessionOptions (record them in the JSON); determinism then becomes a 0-tolerance test on the same config, while ±0.1 AP stays only for a different host or backend.

[Reproducible evaluation, ARH 9.2] 'pycocotools / faster-coco-eval' leaves the metric implementation unfixed, and the two can differ slightly. Pick a single implementation and version for the gate (the other at most as a cross-check), likewise for lvis-api, jiwer/normalizer and pyannote.metrics, and record them in software:{}. Also specify the batch size for accuracy runs (forced max_batch=1, or production micro-batching): batched GEMM can change floating-point results, and accuracy and latency must say which config they used.

[Latency, ARH 9.1/6.4] Latency is measured on the set's images (COCO JPEG ~640x480), while live traffic sends 1920x1440 yuv420f binary through X-Eva-Input, with the YUV→RGB conversion and letterbox done in the engine process. p50/p95 and the ensemble gate (1500 ms) therefore do not describe the live path. Add a mandatory latency run on a fixed, live-shaped input (1920x1440 yuv420f, and 48 kHz f32 audio for audio), separate from the accuracy run. Also clarify whether latency_status='noisy' is accepted by the gate (the single pinned|unpinned|noisy field mixes pinning with noise; split it into pinned:bool + noisy:bool and state the gate rule).

[Interface, INTERFATA 2.1] Precedence is ambiguous when a request has an explicit engine and ensemble='default' while an ensemble is active: does the explicit engine win or the ensemble? State it explicitly (an explicit engine implies ensemble off). Also define the provenance shape for the consumers' local fallback results (engine_id 'local:<file>', the file's sha256, license_set), so that persisted observations stay consistently traceable even when model-server is down.

[Internal consistency] Numeric examples are inconsistent: Engine.resources.threads=8 and provenance.threads=8 against manifest threads=4; the SSE server event shows memBudgetMb 20480 against MODEL_SERVER_MEM_BUDGET_MB=14336 (1.2). Align them so that consumers and the iOS UI do not copy wrong values.

[Feasibility, minor] The segment encoder LRU (16 embeddings per engine; for SAM2-L, ~4-20 MB each with the high-res features) is not included in ram_mb_est/peak. Declare it in the manifest or limit it in MB. For SVT-AV1/x265 at 1920x1440 in codec-worker (4g), memory per preset must be measured; slow presets can exceed 4 GB with several jobs in parallel. Specify codec-worker job concurrency.

Objects365 ('academic purpose only' in the publisher's own terms) is a flag: unclear, so research. The robotics plan (PLAN_FINAL.md, PLAN_V2.md, vision-robotics.md) still names YOLO26 (AGPL) as the Core ML candidate for the phone. Add an explicit ban plus a check in the iOS build pipeline (manifest of bundled models ⊆ production set). (2) B-LIC-1 covers only the server worker (dfine_m_obj365). Nothing requires an inventory of the 'current baseline' detector already shipped in the App Store app, which may itself be Obj365- or AGPL-derived. Add B-LIC-2 with a deadline: an ondevice.* manifest for every model currently in the shipped app, with a licence decision, before deploy.

[M] Unverified ('E') rows can reach production. The recommended default production set (§3) is mostly E: SAM 2.1, MobileSAM, YAMNet, PANNs (weights licence unconfirmed), BEATs, EfficientAT, DINOv2, SigLIP2, Silero, Whisper, Vosk, all codecs. The validator only stops commercial=yes when lineage_flags is non-empty. Setting `legal_review.status=pending` 'if there is any doubt' is subjective and does not stop enabling. Required: mandatory manifest fields `license.verified = {by, at, code_url@commit, weights_url@revision, model_card_url@revision}`. The validator rejects commercial=yes without them, and canEnable returns `license_unverified` until they are present. Add a T21 case for this.

[M] Licences of the software stack in the containers are missing: no SBOM, no licence scan. The matrix covers models, codecs and the main backends, but not the transitive dependencies of the images. Examples: RTAB-Map with g2o/GTSAM/libpointmatcher and the OpenCV it ships with; NeMo/transformers/detectron2/mmdet/sherpa-onnx with their pip dependencies; apt packages. Specific case: §H says RTAB-Map runs in the 'official introlab3it container' with 'nonfree modules disabled'. With the official image you do not control build flags, so you must verify that its OpenCV/RTAB-Map do not include xfeatures2d nonfree (SURF/SIFT-patent) or GPL parts, or build your own image. Propose syft/scancode per image in CI and generate THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES from it as well (needed anyway for G-iOS/G-Robot).

[L] Official source for RT-DETRv2: the weights are cited from HF `PekingU/rtdetr_v2_*`. Check that this HF organisation is controlled by the authors (lyuwenyu/Baidu) and is not the transformers integration upload. Otherwise the primary source is the lyuwenyu/RT-DETR GitHub release (rtdetrv2_pytorch) and the HF upload becomes a conversion, which falls under §0.5/§9 with parity. Separately, the row is marked V without commit/URL for the weights.

[L] HGNetv2 (D-FINE/DEIM, the production default) uses PaddleClas SSLD/stage1 initialisations. Their lineage (distillation with extra data mined from ImageNet-22k, the teacher's training data) should be recorded explicitly in lineage_evidence at pin, not covered only generically by R-IMAGENET. The same goes for 'Apache-2.0 declared' on the weights in Peterande/storage (digest null ⇒ tofu): the source of the weights licence (README line at commit) should be written into the row.

[H][memorie/evaluare, verificat pe server] Doc-ul spune ca memory.peak se reseteaza prin scriere de la kernel >= 5.19 (MODELE_ARHITECTURA §5.4, §9.1, §2.4). Gresit. Resetarea prin scriere exista abia de la kernel 6.12, iar serverul ruleaza 6.8.0-139. In plus, /sys/fs/cgroup e montat read-only in container: proba cu `echo 0 > /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.peak` a dat 'Read-only file system'. Consecinta: in model-server-eval, valoarea cgroup_peak_mb a fiecarui motor este de fapt maximul cumulat pe toata viata containerului, deci include motoarele masurate inainte. Remediu: recreezi containerul model-server-eval pentru fiecare motor/ansamblu (docker compose up --force-recreate cerut de harness prin up.sh) sau esantionezi memory.current/anon la 20 ms. memory.peak se scoate din specificatie pana la kernel >= 6.12.

[H][memorie, verificat] T4(f) cere ca suma PSS a proceselor sa fie <= used (anon+shmem). Pe server, criteriul pica deja pe un proces trivial: Pss total 423 kB, din care Pss_File 367 kB, fata de anon de 116 kB in cgroup. PSS include paginile de fisier mapate (libonnxruntime, libopenvino, numpy), iar acestea nu intra in used. Corect este suma (Pss_Anon + Pss_Shmem), din smaps_rollup. Atribuirea per motor ar trebui raportata tot pe aceste campuri, nu pe Pss total.

[M][memorie] used = anon + shmem lasa pe dinafara memoria kernel din memory.stat (kernel, slab, pagetables, sock, kernel_stack), desi ea intra in memory.max. Cu zeci de procese spawn si sute de fire (pids_limit 1024), ea poate ajunge la sute de MB, deci OOM-ul poate veni inainte ca bugetul de admitere sa fie atins. Remediu: includ 'kernel' in used sau scad o rezerva masurata din MODEL_SERVER_MEM_BUDGET_MB.

[H][fuziune statistica] §6.5 si MODELE_INTERFATA §2.2 afirma ca individualul calibrat si ansamblul au 'aceeasi scara'. Pentru WBF afirmatia nu tine: media scorurilor calibrate din cluster, cu penalizarea pentru membrii absenti (conf*min(n,T)/n), nu mai este o probabilitate calibrata. Nici media ponderata a probabilitatilor calibrate nu e calibrata in general (iese subconfidenta). Pragurile consumatorilor si-ar schimba deci sensul tocmai la comutarea pe ansamblu. Remediu: un fisier de calibrare propriu al iesirii ansamblului, invatat pe val-A dupa fuziune; score_semantics=calibrated@<sha-ul acestui fisier>, iar T26 se reformuleaza (acum spune 'acelasi sha de fisier per membru', ceea ce e ambiguu).

[H][fuziune statistica] Supraajustare per clasa: ponderile WBF per (model, clasa), selectia best_per_class si calibrarea per (model, clasa) se invata pe val-A, care are 250 de imagini COCO. Multe din cele 80 de clase au acolo sub 5 instante. AP per clasa pe val-A nu poate alege modelul in mod robust. Remediu: prag minim de instante per clasa (ex. >= 20), sub prag fallback pe ponderea sau temperatura globala a modelului; contractie (shrinkage) spre parametrul global; sau val-A mai mare (ex. toate imaginile filtrate pe licenta, cu o mie de imagini pentru val-A). Acelasi lucru la audio: Platt per clasa pe 527 de clase AudioSet pe subsetul FSD50K CC0/CC-BY, cu numar minim de pozitive si fallback.

[H][poarta ansamblului, multiplicitate] §6.4 nu fixeaza cate configuratii candidate (mod x subset de membri) se testeaza pe val-B. Daca se testeaza toate si se activeaza oricare are CI95_low > 0, rata de fals pozitiv creste cu numarul de candidati. Se adauga refolosirea lui val-B la fiecare model nou (§9.4), care duce la supraajustare adaptiva. Remediu: alegerea unui SINGUR candidat per sarcina doar pe val-A, testat apoi o singura data pe val-B; sau corectie Holm/Bonferroni peste candidati; plus un test inghetat, folosit rar.

[M][poarta ansamblului] Bootstrap-ul nu e specificat complet. Trebuie spus ca e bootstrap pereche (aceleasi imagini reesantionate pentru ansamblu si pentru individual) si cum se trateaza max_m: individualul fixat ales pe val-A, sau recalculat in fiecare reesantionare. Cu max_m luat pe val-B fara reguli, se amesteca doua efecte de selectie. Esantionarea trebuie facuta pe clustere: uploader Freesound la FSD50K, vorbitor la LibriSpeech/Common Voice; clipurile aceluiasi uploader/vorbitor sunt corelate si CI-ul iese prea ingust. Split-ul val-A/val-B la audio trebuie facut tot pe uploader. Auto-dezactivarea (§6.4) are nevoie de histerezis (ex. dezactivare doar daca CI95_high < 0 sau la doua rulari consecutive), altfel ansamblul oscileaza la zgomot.

[H][evaluare, contaminare] Seturile de poarta nu au o verificare de contaminare intre antrenare si evaluare. (1) LVIS v1 val (19.8k imagini) contine in mare parte imagini din COCO train2017. Detectoarele COCO (D-FINE, RT-DETR, DEIM etc.) si mapările lvis_to_coco80 sunt atunci evaluate pe imagini de antrenare; trebuie restrans la intersectia cu COCO val2017 (verifica pe adnotari). (2) CLAP: MS-CLAP a declarat FSD50K in antrenare, iar LAION-Audio-630K provine in mare parte din Freesound, deci clipurile din FSD50K eval pot fi vazute la antrenare. Inainte de poarta trebuie deduplicat dupa ID-ul Freesound sau CLAP trebuie exclus. Recomand un camp dataset.contamination_check in eva.benchmark/1 si o regula: membrii cu contaminare necontrolata nu intra in poarta.

[M][reproductibilitate vs productie] §9.5 cere ORT_DISABLE_ALL pentru metricile de acuratete. Asta contrazice 'aceeasi cale de cod ca in productie' (§9.1) si schimba numeric graful fata de productie, unde optimizarile sunt activate. Rezultatul: AP-ul raportat si fisierele de calibrare invatate pe val-A provin din alta configuratie decat cea servita live. Pe CPU, ORT cu fire fixe si optimizari de graf (deterministe) e deja reproductibil. Remediu: acuratetea si latenta se masoara cu exact optiunile de sesiune din productie, iar acestea se noteaza in eva.benchmark/1 (graph_optimization_level, threads).

[M][latenta, fezabilitate CPU] Latenta folosita de poarta (bugetul p95 pentru ansamblu) se masoara in model-server-eval: cpuset 0-3, cpus = 4 (fara throttling CFS), threads din plan. In productie e altfel: cpuset 8-15 cu cota cpus 6 (cu throttling CFS cand 8+ fire ruleaza pe o cota de 6), motoarele 'pornite pentru comparatie' au threads:1, iar membrii ansamblului nu se stie daca ruleaza secvential sau in paralel. Cifra din eval nu reprezinta latenta live a ansamblului. Remediu: planul de evaluare reproduce exact threads/afinitatea/ordinea membrilor din productie; se defineste executia membrilor (paralel cu afinitati disjuncte sau secvential); poarta foloseste latenta in configuratia de productie.

[M][fezabilitate CPU] Lipseste un model de capacitate pentru fluxul live. Admiterea se uita doar la suma threads <= 1,5 x cpus, nu la cererea reala: cadre/s x ms-CPU masurati per motor. Un ansamblu cu N membri consuma ~N x CPU pe cerere, iar poarta verifica doar latenta, nu si throughput-ul sub rata live (keyframes la 5 fps + audio continuu + SAM pe detectii) in cota de 6 CPU. Remediu: evaluatorul masoara cpu_ms_per_request si throughput-ul sustinut; poarta ansamblului si activarea implicitelor verifica rata_live x cpu_ms <= cota disponibila, nu doar p95.

[M][fezabilitate CPU, evaluator] Vocabularul deschis pe LVIS cu cele 1203 clase complete nu e estimat pe CPU. Grounding DINO/MM-GDINO trebuie sa imparta vocabularul in bucati (limita de 256 de tokeni), adica zeci de inferente pe imagine, deci ore per model pentru 300 de imagini pe 4 CPU. La VLM-uri (Qwen3-VL, Florence-2) vocabularul complet e practic infezabil. Trebuie specificate: strategia de impartire, un buget de timp per rulare si, pentru motoarele lente, un subset fix de vocabular, notat in dataset.subset_sha256. In plus, o estimare a duratei totale a evaluarii complete pe CPU-ul serverului.

[M][interfata, izolarea resurselor] Gateway-ul accepta corpuri binare de pana la 64 MB, cu MODEL_SERVER_MAX_INFLIGHT=32 si max_queue 32 per motor. In cel mai rau caz asta inseamna peste 2 GB de corpuri tinute in memoria gateway-ului, fata de o rezerva de 1536 MB pentru gateway+fusion+pipe-uri. Lipseste o admitere pe octeti in asteptare (ex. MODEL_SERVER_MAX_PENDING_BYTES), cu 429/413 peste limita. Mai e o problema: Connection.send_bytes pe pipe e blocant (buffer de pipe de 64 KB), deci un transfer de 4-64 MB din bucla async blocheaza toate motoarele. Remediu: multiprocessing.shared_memory cu predare de handle, sau transferul ruleaza in executor/thread dedicat; T24 sa masoare si acest caz.

[M][provenienta] Lipsesc doua elemente pentru reproducerea unei predictii. (a) input_sha256: hash-ul octetilor de intrare, calculat in procesul motorului; ref e opac si optional. (b) Parametrii efectivi ai cererii (score_threshold, max_detections, label_space, beam_size, vad_filter etc.) sau un params_sha256 canonic. Fara ele, doua rezultate cu aceeasi provenienta nu pot fi reproduse. image_digest injectat de up.sh din 'docker image inspect': imaginile construite local nu au RepoDigest, deci trebuie specificat .Id (digest-ul de config), iar fara up.sh valoarea sa fie explicit 'unknown', nu goala. git_sha are nevoie si de un steag git_dirty la build.

[L][interfata, izolare] version explicit in cerere (MODELE_INTERFATA §2.1) permite oricarui consumator sa incarce in model-server live o versiune neactiva, 'daca bugetul permite'. Asta ocoleste starea dorita stabilita de admin si consuma din bugetul motoarelor implicite, fara audit. Remediu: versiunile neactive se servesc doar cu X-Eva-Purpose eval/replay de la apelantii listati, sau doar daca adminul le-a permis explicit; incarcarea se trece in audit cu actor=system.

[L][fuziune] Mapările many-to-one (o365_to_coco80, lvis_to_coco80) nu spun cum se combina scorurile mai multor clase sursa care cad pe aceeasi clasa COCO pe aceeasi caseta (max, suma probabilitatilor sau NMS inainte de WBF). Alegerea schimba AP-ul si trebuie fixata in labelmap si testata in T6. Pentru FSD50K trebuie specificata si propagarea pe ierarhia AudioSet: FSD50K are etichete pe noduri intermediare, iar predictiile pe frunze trebuie urcate la stramosi (max) inainte de mAP. Mai e o nepotrivire: §6.3 descrie o temperatura per model (sigma(T_m*logit)), iar §6.5 descrie Platt per (motor, clasa) pentru audio; una din ele trebuie aleasa.

[L][operare] La transcribe (600 s), regula 'procesul motorului se reporneste daca nu raspunde in 2 x timeout' (§5.4) inseamna ca un proces blocat tine coada pana la 20 de minute. Pentru detectia blocajului e nevoie de un heartbeat separat al procesului motorului (ex. ping pe pipe la 5 s), independent de timeout-ul cererii.

It edits three files: Site/docs/MODELE_ARHITECTURA.md, Site/docs/MODELE_LICENTE.md and Site/docs/MODELE_INTERFATA.md. These are document changes only; no code was written and nothing was run. All 14 audit points are answered, and the table in MODELE_ARHITECTURA §19.3 maps each one to where it is fixed.

LICENCES
(1) One checkable rule now decides flag versus residual risk (MODELE_LICENTE §0.1.1). Every dataset is classified by the text of its own publisher's terms, recorded as terms_class in dataset_classes.json. Non-commercial or academic-only terms produce a flag. The single exception is when the weights licensor owns the dataset. Commercial-use labels with third-party rights on each image or clip produce a residual-risk class.
- The rule is applied to every row. ImageNet becomes the flag restricted_data_terms:imagenet-* and R-IMAGENET is withdrawn. SA-1B stays R-SA1B only for Meta's weights (SAM 1/2, EdgeTAM). For third-party models it is a flag: MobileSAM, EfficientViT-SAM, Light HQ-SAM, and EfficientSAM until its licensor is proven.
- Flags pass from teacher to student by the same rule as for OWLv2. A new flag withdrawn_data covers LAION-2B.
- The owner can approve several engines in one signed note that covers one flag for one dataset (for example imagenet-backbones).
(2) The production set is split into three tiers:
- P0 has no flags. It covers YOLOX, SigLIP2, YAMNet, PANNs, BEATs, Silero, Whisper, Vosk, the codecs, reconstruction and the inference backends.
- P1 needs the owner's ImageNet note. It adds D-FINE COCO, DEIM, RT-DETR, RTMDet, Detic, SAM 2, DINOv2 and AST.
- P2 also needs an SA-1B note for the third-party segmenters.
- Consequence: without the owner's ImageNet note, production has no segmenter and no open-vocabulary detector, and the closed-set detector is YOLOX. B-LIC-1 is updated to reflect this.
(3) Every manifest must now carry license.verified (who checked, when, and the code, weights and model-card URLs pinned to a commit or revision). Without it the validator rejects commercial=yes and the engine reports license_unverified.
(4) Distribution is covered:
- Every manifest gets deploy_targets (server, robot, ios).
- A new G-Robot section sets what may ship on robots: only an LGPL ffmpeg build; no R-PATENT codecs; NVIDIA libraries only after their distribution clause is read; no research engines, so SAM 3.1 cannot be used in b15's semantic-inference service.
- Risk acceptances are now recorded per target.
- On iOS, nothing non-commercial or unclear may be in the App Store binary at all, even disabled. The build must pass check_bundle.py. YOLO26 (AGPL) is banned without a paid licence.
- New blocker B-LIC-2, deadline 2026-10-14: an inventory and licence decision for every model already shipped in the iOS app.
(5) Every container image gets an SBOM (syft) and a licence scan (scancode), checked against a per-target policy, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES is generated from them for each target. RTAB-Map runs in production only from an image we build ourselves.
(6) RT-DETRv2: I checked the HF PekingU model card. Those weights were contributed by the transformers integration, not by the authors. The primary source is now the lyuwenyu/RT-DETR GitHub release, and the weights column is marked E (to verify).
(7) The PaddleClas SSLD ImageNet lineage of HGNetv2 is now recorded explicitly, as is the README line that declares the D-FINE weights licence.

MEMORY
- memory.peak is dropped. Kernel 6.8 cannot reset it and /sys/fs/cgroup is read-only. Instead, the eval container is recreated for each engine or ensemble and memory is sampled every 20 ms.
- The memory budget now counts anon + shmem + kernel + sock.
- Per-engine attribution uses Pss_Anon + Pss_Shmem.

STATISTICS
- Each ensemble gets its own calibration file, fitted after fusion, and ECE is measured.
- The gate set is now every COCO val2017 image with licence 4-8 (estimated about 1,400-1,700; the exact count is recorded when the set is fetched). It is split into A1/A2/B/C, with per-class parameters only above 20 instances and shrinkage below that. The audio set works the same way.
- The ensemble gate:
  - Only one pre-registered candidate per task is tested on val-B.
  - The bootstrap is paired, with the best single model recomputed in each replicate.
  - A Bonferroni correction applies across each gate epoch.
  - A frozen val-C confirms the result.
- Tests T4, T5, T7, T8, T21, T23, T26 and T28 are extended; T29, T30 and T31 are new.

STILL OPEN
- The task list I received was cut off in the middle of item 14 (bootstrap); I resolved it from the readable part. Anything after it was not seen.
- Owner decisions still needed: B-LIC-1 and B-LIC-2, both due 2026-10-14; whether to sign the imagenet-backbones and sa1b-third-party notes; and acceptance of the residual-risk classes for each target.
- I did not edit PLAN_FINAL.md, PLAN_V2.md, vision-robotics.md or any b15 files. Their corrections go through coordination notes owned by platform.

[H][provenance/fusion] composite_sha256 is circular and too fragile. Per §5.6 and MODELE_INTERFATA §2.2 it includes calibration_sha256 (the calibration file for the ensemble's output). But §6.5 stores that file under model_store/calibration/ensemble/<task>/<composite_sha256>/, so you need the hash to find the file and the file to compute the hash. composite_sha256 also includes server_build {git_sha, image_digest}. That means any image rebuild changes it, including platform commits unrelated to the ensemble. A test-stack image (:models-test) or a model-server-eval image never has the live image's digest either. As a result, the pre-registration and gate evidence (§6.4, E4 'diferită de candidatul preînregistrat' -> 409) can never match the live combination, and nothing says what happens to an active ensemble after a redeploy. Fix: separate the content hash (method, params, weights, members, member and output calibration, adapter.source_sha256) from the build. Put server_build only in provenance, key the calibration file by the content hash without the output calibration, and state an explicit gate-validity rule across rebuilds (for example, re-validate when adapter.source_sha256 or the backend version changes).

[H][CPU/memory feasibility] Memory admission ignores weights that are mmapped from files. OpenVINO 2024+ mmaps the IR .bin by default (ENABLE_MMAP), and ORT can mmap external initializers. Those pages show up in memory.stat as file/file_mapped (field confirmed on the server), not as anon. §5.4 leaves them out of used and keeps only a 512 MB page-cache reserve. As written, you can admit engines whose anon fits in 14336 MB but whose actively used mmapped weights push the cgroup past mem_limit 16g. The kernel then reclaims and refaults those pages on every inference, latency collapses (thrashing), there is no OOM, and no error is reported. Fix: either force loading into anon (ov ENABLE_MMAP=false, ORT loading from bytes/no mmap) and declare it in runtime.memory, or count file_mapped/active_file of each engine's weights in admission. Add a test: an engine with mmapped weights larger than the reserve gets refused or counted.

[M][measurement reproducibility] Sampling smaps_rollup at 20 ms on the engine process runs at the same time as the latency measurement (§9.1). For a process with a large address space, smaps_rollup walks the whole VMA tree under mmap_lock and blocks the engine's allocations/page faults, which inflates p95. Split it into separate passes: (a) memory with 20 ms sampling, (b) latency with no sampling, or a light sampler only on memory.stat. Also state that the sampled peak is a lower bound (short ORT optimization transients get missed) and add a safety margin in admission.

[M][latency gate not representative] The ensemble gate requires p95 <= latency_budget_ms measured in model-server-eval (cpuset 0-3, cpus 4). In production the members run in model-server (cpuset 8-15, cpus 6, thread cap 1.5x6=9 shared with the other loaded engines, disjoint affinity subsets). For an ensemble whose members together have more than 4 threads, the eval violates the invariant 'threads <= CPUs in the cpuset' (D19) and is oversubscribed, so the measured latency is neither valid nor predictive for production. Fix: give eval a thread/affinity plan identical to the production one (cpuset size >= sum of member threads, or member threads scaled the same way in both places), and record the plan in eva.benchmark/1.

[M][threads as a manifest property] threads is fixed in the manifest. §5.4 asks that engines 'pornite pentru comparație' (started for comparison) run with threads:1 and the default with <=4. An engine that becomes the default from Settings keeps threads:1, and the benchmark/UI shows the latency for a single thread count. Fix: threads should be desired runtime configuration per role (default / comparison / ensemble member), applied by the reconciler and written into provenance.threads, with benchmarks per measured thread count. Otherwise the selector compares engines under different conditions.

[M][fusion statistics: audio] Platt calibration and the audio gate are computed on FSD50K, which has clip-level (weak) labels, so they are pooled scores. But classify_audio returns frames on a 0.48 s grid, with the 10 s windows (AST/PaSST) max-pooled onto the grid (§6.3). Platt parameters learned on clip scores do not calibrate frame scores, and the ensemble's frame-level fusion is never evaluated. Fix: declare score_semantics=calibrated only on result.clip, keep frames raw (or calibrate them on a frame-labeled set, e.g. strong-label AudioSet/DESED, if the license allows), and state explicitly that the audio gate covers clip-level fusion only.

[M][fusion statistics: detection] The event being calibrated is undefined. Temperature/ECE for detection requires 'correct detection' to be defined: the IoU threshold (0.5? the average over .5:.95?), class-matched greedy matching as in COCO, and the effect of score_threshold/max_detections on the population of detections. Without it, ECE <= 0.05 in the gate (§6.4) and T26 are not reproducible across implementations. Specify it (e.g. TP = class-matched, IoU >= 0.5, COCO greedy matching, all detections with score >= 0.05, top-100 per image, 15 bins), plus the D-ECE variant if used.

[M][evaluator reproducibility vs production] §9.5 runs accuracy with ORT_DISABLE_ALL 'unde se aplică' (where applicable), while production presumably uses the default optimizations. Benchmark numbers, calibration files and gate evidence would then come from a different numerical graph than the one serving live traffic, which contradicts 'aceeași cale de cod ca în producție' (the same code path as production, §9.1). Fix: measure in the production configuration (fixed graph_optimization_level, fixed threads, deterministic on CPU with a fixed thread count), record the level in provenance/benchmark, and keep ORT_DISABLE_ALL only for a separate determinism test.

[M][evaluation contamination] The evaluation images are not checked against the models' training sets. LVIS v1 minival contains images from COCO 2017, including train2017, so COCO/LVIS-trained models (D-FINE, DEIM, RT-DETR, Detic) can be evaluated on images they were trained on. Some ODinW sub-sets also overlap with public training sets. Require a dedup step against each model's declared training set IDs (license.data[]), with a 'contaminated' flag and exclusion from the gate.

[M][isolation of the test/eval stack] (1) §1.2 says up.sh is the only sanctioned way to start, yet §15 'Pornire izolată' runs docker compose up directly, bypassing the guard. (2) The guard 'refuză orice serviciu fără mem_limit/memswap_limit/cpuset/cpus/cpu_shares/pids_limit' (refuses any service without them), but in the test project it also starts the compose.yaml services (db, migrate, content, app, worker), which have no limits at all. Either the test stack can never start through up.sh, or there is an undocumented exception. (3) up -d --build without selecting services also starts worker (image eva-3d-scan-worker:local, rebuilt), and the base image eva-3d-scan-site:local has build: . in x-site-image. The :models-test override must cover app, migrate, content and worker explicitly, or the services must be listed explicitly in the command. Otherwise the live tags get overwritten, which is exactly lesson D12. Add test T22b: after the test stack starts, docker image inspect eva-3d-scan-site:local / eva-3d-scan-worker:local shows the same digest as before.

[L][bootstrap feasibility] 1000 paired replicas x (ensemble + all production individuals), with a full COCO mAP recomputation per replica on val-B, run in the harness with cpus 1 (cpuset 20-21). With pycocotools that is hours per gate. Specify the method: precompute per-image matches at each IoU threshold once, then rebuild only the PR curves per replica (or use faster-coco-eval), and state the measured time budget.

[L][gate/latency] latency_status has a single value 'pinned|unpinned|noisy', but a run can be both pinned and noisy, and the gate does not say whether a noisy latency can satisfy p95 <= budget. Split it into pinned:bool + noisy:bool and state the gate rule explicitly (e.g. noisy => latency condition not_run => the ensemble stays pending_benchmark).

[L][interface] Overloading provenance.manifest_sha256 with composite_sha256 for an ensemble changes the field's meaning: a manifest lookup by sha in model_engine_versions fails. Also, on an ensemble, the top-level provenance fields weights_sha256/backend/threads/precision/adapter have no defined value. Define them explicitly (null or a list from members) and add a provenance.kind:'single|ensemble' discriminator so consumers do not have to infer it from the 'ensemble:' prefix.

findings.description: Provenance of committed benchmarks is broken. In 22 of the vision benchmark JSONs (44 counting the copies under docs/benchmarks), engine.manifest_sha256 does not match the canonical hash of the manifest in c0d6dd0. In 28 of 49, adapter.source_sha256 does not match the adapter source in the commit. Affected: rtdetrv2.s, yolox.m/s/nano/tiny on all splits, and all segmenters. Cause: run_detect_eval hashes the whole manifest, including mutable fields (verified.at, resources.ram_*, backends_parity). Writing measurements back into the manifest therefore changes the hash. Three of the five detection-ensemble members (rtdetrv2.s, yolox.m, yolox.s) are stale, so composite_sha256 / prereg reference artifacts that no longer exist. MODELE_INTERFATA says results with a different adapter.source_sha256 are not directly comparable, yet the §2 table and the ensemble mix them. report.py --check does not detect any of this. For yolox.s the numbers do reproduce with the current code (identical mAP), but the recorded chain does not.

Peak RAM is not reproducible, and the admission limits written into manifests are too low. On re-run, accuracy matches exactly but memory does not. dfine.n-coco: peak_load 456 vs 330 MB, steady 406 vs 230 MB. yolox.s: peak_load 283-302 vs 189 MB. The cause is the 'process minus harness baseline' measurement in a shared process, which depends on the order of engines in the batch. These values go into MODELE_BENCHMARK ('Memorie MB' column) and into resources.ram_mb_peak_load. yolox.s declares 236 MB, but re-measurement gives 283-302 MB. The tolerance spec in repro.py / §9.5 does not cover memory at all, and only segmenters are flagged as unrealistic in §9.2.4. Detectors are affected too and are not disclosed.
findings.location: Site/models/eval/vision/run_detect_eval.py (Sampler / base subtraction); Site/models/registry/detect/detect.yolox.s/1.0.0.json resources; Site/docs/MODELE_BENCHMARK.md §2 'Memorie MB' column

findings.description: The test 'memory limits respected' is order-dependent and fails in isolation. test_memory_after_warmup_within_manifest_peak[detect.dfine.m-obj365@1.0.0] fails when run alone: 805 MB and 868 MB against a declared ram_mb_peak_load of 767 MB (default_2.5x). It passes only in the full suite, because modules loaded earlier inflate the baseline that gets subtracted. The reported pass does not prove the limit holds.

The detection gate tested a degenerate candidate, and the report describes it misleadingly. The best_per_class candidate chosen on val-A2 selects detect.dfine.m-coco for all 79 classes (Counter of params.choice), so it is m* itself. Its val-A2 score (54.302) equals m* exactly. The single val-B test (k=1) therefore compared m* with m* plus Platt output recalibration: Delta -0.13 AP comes only from recalibration, and no real combination was tested. MODELE_BENCHMARK §3 presents it as 'mod best_per_class cu 5 membri' with 'ansamblu 55.08 vs 55.21', i.e. as evidence the combination loses. The tie between a candidate identical to m* and m* should have produced 'no candidate beats m* on val-A2, no val-B test'. Methodological leak in the selection: best_per_class uses ap2 (val-A2) to build its choice, then is ranked on the same val-A2 against WBF candidates scored out-of-sample, which biases selection toward bpc. val-B stays clean (loaded after the prereg; checked in code).
findings.location: Site/models/eval/vision/ensemble_eval.py:186-200 (best_per_class + pick); Site/models/fusion/selection.py:8-25; Site/docs/MODELE_BENCHMARK.md lines 74-77 and summary row 18

findings.description: Audio gate: the preregistration is not written before val-B is read, contrary to the docstring. Member val-B metrics (mAP, lwlrap, ECE) are computed in the same loop as the val-A1 calibration, before candidate selection. The prereg exists only in memory and lands in the same output file after the val-B test (no separate file, no prior timestamp, unlike ensemble_eval.py). Candidate selection does use only A1/A2 (checked in code: no actual leak), and the result reproduces exactly. The 'prereg before val-B' guarantee cannot be audited.

findings.description: reproducibility.json cannot be regenerated from the repo. The repro.py spec (spec.json) and the run1/run2 files it compares are not committed. report.py --check only re-reads the committed JSON, so the 'passed: true' verdict cannot be verified by an auditor except by re-running by hand (which I did: the numbers match).

During the transcribe run (whisper.tiny), ONNX Runtime tries to pin threads to cores outside the container cpuset: 'pthread_setaffinity_np failed ... mask {23}'. Some ORT session in the audio path does not set intra_op_num_threads explicitly and creates threads for every core on the host. That oversubscribes the declared --cpus limit and makes the latency context less faithful. WER is unaffected.
findings.location: Site/models/eval/speech/speech_eval.py transcribe / Site/models/adapters/audio (ORT session without explicit threads)

findings.description: The vision tests depend on export/vision/testdata (gitignored, re-downloaded from coco_url) and on COCO annotations. In a clean clone without them, 36 tests come out as 'skipped', including T3 (honest error on missing weights) and backend parity. The skip is honest and has a reason, but run_tests/README give no single command that fetches the data offline from the eva-models-eval-data volume. The audit had to copy the 4 images by hand; their sha256 matched ATTRIBUTION.json.

result.verdict: The accuracy figures reproduce exactly when I re-run them on the server's CPU, but the branch is not merge-ready on reproducibility grounds. Re-runs in separate containers matched to delta 0: D-FINE n and YOLOX s on val-B, Whisper tiny WER, Silero VAD, the audio gate at k=2, and the lossless codecs (bit-exact, 28/28 rows). All suites pass: evaluator 8, platform 99, audio 249, vision+backends 194 plus 24. report --check is deterministic. Four major findings: (1) the recorded provenance is broken: 22 benchmarks cite a manifest_sha256 and 28 an adapter.source_sha256 that do not exist in the commit, because the manifest hash covers fields that get rewritten; (2) peak RAM is not reproducible (+38% to +76%), it depends on the order of engines in the harness, and it is written into manifests as an admission limit that is too low (yolox.s 236 declared vs 283-302 measured); (3) the memory-limit test fails in isolation for dfine.m-obj365 (805-868 MB > 767) and passes only because of test order; (4) the detection gate tested a candidate identical to m* (best_per_class = dfine.m-coco on all 79 classes), so the reported Delta -0.13 does not measure a combination. Selection on val-A2 also favors bpc in-sample. val-B stays clean. Minor: the audio prereg exists only in memory, after val-B metrics are computed (no actual leak); the reproducibility spec and inputs are not committed; ORT affinity spills outside the cpuset. No compose stack was needed (there is no model-server yet): everything ran in standalone containers named aud1-*, --network none, no host ports, with cpu/memory limits. The clone ~/work/3dscan-modaudit1 and the temp directories were deleted, and the weights volumes were not touched.
